note: The two sets are nearly identical; the only differences are two material-property claims where B binds the values to 'tower steel' and keeps the 'Table 4-1' condition, while A uses the vaguer entity 'steel' and drops the condition. Both sets share the same defects: a misread 0.18 Hz tower natural frequency alongside a 0.17 Hz claim and a 0.170 Hz claim (the same fact stated three times), and 1P/3P frequency ranges whose quotes are only legend labels. Both also leave out notable facts such as the 7% outfitting mass, the 100 t transition piece, and the stiffer-tower requirement for a floating substructure. B is marginally more faithful, but the gap is small.
remarks: Both sets report the tower's first natural frequency three times (0.18 Hz, 0.17 Hz, 0.170 Hz); the text states 0.170 Hz and the figure line is at ~0.17 Hz, so 0.18 Hz is a misread and the 0.17/0.170 entries are duplicates. The 1P (0.09-0.13 Hz) and 3P (0.25-0.38 Hz) ranges appear to be estimates read off the shaded bands of Figure 4-1; the quoted legend labels do not support those numeric ranges. Facts on the page that neither set captures: 7% outfitting mass beyond the cylindrical shell mass, 100 t for the transition piece, soil modeled as spring constants in a 1-D FE model (values representative of dense sand or gravel), and the note that a floating substructure requires a stiffer tower.
